warrantyBasic: Data unavailable: Bugatti's Tourbillon warranty terms have not been publicly itemized as of 2026-05-21. The Chiron-era warranty was typically 4-year unlimited-mileage with optional extensions and a separate paid-maintenance program.
warrantyBattery: Data unavailable: Rimac-supplied high-voltage battery warranty terms for the Tourbillon have not been publicly disclosed.
driverAssistBrand: Data unavailable: no named ADAS suite branding (no equivalent to Super Cruise, BlueCruise, or Highway Drive Assist) announced for the Tourbillon.
infotainment: Bespoke Bugatti infotainment system with a fully analog instrument cluster and a hidden retractable touchscreen that emerges from the center stack. Designed to favor mechanical instruments over screens. Specific software platform, processor, and head unit vendor not publicly disclosed. Source: https://newsroom.bugatti.com/en/press-releases/the-bugatti-tourbillon-an-automotive-icon-pour-leternite
adasStandard: Data unavailable: Bugatti has not published a detailed ADAS feature list for the Tourbillon. Hypercars at this price point typically include basic driver aids (ABS, ESC, traction control, tire-pressure monitoring) but are not marketed on ADAS feature parity with mainstream luxury vehicles. No public confirmation of adaptive cruise, lane-keep assist, or AEB as standard.
adasOptional: Data unavailable: no public optional ADAS package list for the Tourbillon as of 2026-05-21.
rearViewCameraNotes: Data unavailable: Bugatti has not detailed the rear-view camera resolution, multi-angle capability, or dynamic guideline support for the Tourbillon. Press materials emphasize an analog-instrument dashboard and a hidden retractable center touchscreen for camera/infotainment views. Source: https://newsroom.bugatti.com/en/press-releases/the-bugatti-tourbillon-an-automotive-icon-pour-leternite
sideViewCameraNotes: Data unavailable: no public specification of surround-view 360 cameras, side-blind cameras, or trailer-view systems on the Tourbillon. The car uses traditional exterior mirrors per visible press imagery.
subscriptionFeatures: No subscription-gated features have been announced for the Tourbillon. Bugatti's bespoke-buyer business model (sub-300 unit production runs, hand-built configurations) does not currently use subscription monetization for features like heated seats, ADAS, or performance modes that has surfaced at BMW and Mercedes. Data unavailable: no public infotainment subscription pricing.
drmNotes: The Tourbillon is expected to follow Bugatti's existing 'Connected Car' telemetry model: vehicles transmit operating data to Molsheim for prognostics and service scheduling but do not require permanent internet connectivity to drive. Software updates are performed at authorized Bugatti service centers, not over-the-air to the consumer. No public evidence of remote feature reduction, subscription-gated performance, or DRM-style activation requirements. Source: https://newsroom.bugatti.com/en/press-releases/connected-car-la-bugatti
killSwitchNotes: No impaired-driving-detection kill switch has been announced for the Tourbillon. The IIJA Section 24220 federal mandate has not yet produced a final NHTSA rule (NHTSA reported in early 2026 that available technologies do not meet required accuracy levels), and Bugatti has not published a compliance plan. The Tourbillon's 2026 launch units therefore ship without such a system. Source: https://dallasexpress.com/national/ready-for-your-next-car-to-decide-if-youre-too-impaired-to-drive-federal-kill-switch-is-moving-forward/
knownIssues: Data unavailable: pre-production. The Tourbillon has not yet been delivered to customers as of 2026-05-21 (deliveries begin later in 2026), so no field reliability or known-issue corpus exists.
recalls: None as of 2026-05-21: no NHTSA recall campaigns have been issued for the Tourbillon (vehicle is pre-customer-delivery). Source: https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls
stateIncentives: Not applicable in practice: the Tourbillon's ~$4.1M MSRP and 250-unit global production make it ineligible for or excluded from typical state EV incentive programs (which cap MSRP at $80k or lower in major markets like California's CVRP/CVAP and New York's Drive Clean Rebate). PHEV with only 37 mi EV range also falls below many programs' minimum range thresholds.
